profile.reading:
LightEdge Austin I is a colocation data center at 2916 Montopolis Drive, Suite 300, Austin, Texas 78741, in the Montopolis area of southeast Austin, Travis County, near Austin Bergstrom International Airport. LightEdge's own site and its own published Austin facility fact sheet both confirm this exact address as one of the company's two Austin buildings, resolving an earlier ambiguity in LightEdge's own marketing between this address and the company's second Austin location, at 7000-B Burleson Road, Suite 400, roughly two miles away. Both buildings are described together, rather than separately, in LightEdge's combined Austin market specifications, which state 58,471 total square feet across the two facilities, including 40,960 square feet of technical white space, 2.5 megawatts of critical IT workload capacity, 8.25 megawatts of total generator capacity, and an isolated 2N uninterruptible power supply configuration. Because those power and space figures span both Austin buildings together rather than this one alone, they are treated here as combined market level figures rather than assigned specifically to Austin I, and no separate square footage, IT load, or generator figure specific to this single building was found in any source reviewed. LightEdge's own materials do not disclose a tier rating, a year built, or any named tenant for either Austin facility.

The facility carries a broad, compliance oriented certification set that is common across LightEdge's portfolio, including SOC 1, SOC 2, and SOC 3 attestations, ISO 27001, ISO 20000-1, and ISO 22301 certifications, HITRUST certification, HIPAA and HITECH readiness, PCI DSS compliance, and alignment with the NIST 800-53 and NIST 800-171 federal security frameworks, positioning the site for regulated and government adjacent workloads rather than only hyperscale or wholesale tenancy. LightEdge lists nine on-net network carriers serving its Austin buildings, including AT&T, Cogent Communications, Crown Castle Fiber, FiberLight, Grande Communications, Lumen, Logix, Spectrum, and Zayo.

LightEdge Solutions was founded in 1996 and is headquartered in Des Moines, Iowa. The company announced a new capital partnership with GI Partners, a private equity and real estate investment firm, in September 2021, and underwent a chief executive transition from longtime leader Jim Masterson to Rob Carter effective January 1, 2025. LightEdge describes its current national footprint as twenty data centers across twelve United States metro markets, plus one location in Amsterdam, Netherlands, positioning Austin as one metro within a broader mid market, compliance focused colocation strategy rather than a hyperscale one. Austin has grown rapidly as a Texas technology hub over the past decade, drawing both large hyperscale campuses from other operators and the kind of mid sized, compliance driven colocation demand that LightEdge's business model typically serves, a pattern consistent with the company's decision to maintain two separate buildings in this one metro rather than a single larger campus. No Travis County or City of Austin zoning case, building permit record, or tax abatement filing specific to 2916 Montopolis Drive was found in this research, and no year the facility was built or opened was located in any source reviewed.

reading.body:
LightEdge Austin I is a colocation data center in southeast Austin near the airport, one of two LightEdge buildings in the metro located roughly two miles apart. The operator publishes combined specifications across both Austin buildings but not per building: 2.5 MW of critical IT workload capacity and 8.25 MW of total generator capacity across 58,471 square feet including 40,960 square feet of white space. Without a per-building breakdown, the IT load capable at this single facility cannot be determined from published sources; assuming the 2.5 MW IT capacity were evenly split between two buildings, roughly 1.25 MW would serve this location, which at 40 kW per rack corresponds to approximately 30 racks, though this is an estimate only and LightEdge has not published a per-building figure.

The facility holds compliance certifications typical of mid-market colocation: SOC 1, SOC 2, SOC 3, ISO 27001, ISO 20000-1, ISO 22301, HITRUST, HIPAA and HITECH readiness, and PCI DSS compliance, qualifying it for regulated and government-adjacent workloads rather than hyperscale tenancy alone. Nine network carriers serve the Austin buildings on net, including AT&T, Cogent, Crown Castle Fiber, FiberLight, Grande, Lumen, Logix, Spectrum, and Zayo. LightEdge operates twenty data centers across twelve US metros plus Amsterdam as a mid-market compliance-focused provider rather than a hyperscale operator.

LightEdge Austin I publishes no power capacity specific to this building alone, placing it outside the top 19 published-capacity facilities in Texas by individual facility disclosure. Texas has 133 mapped data center facilities and 475 MW of published IT capacity across 19 disclosed sites, with this facility ranking 20th by the combined Austin market figure of 2.5 MW. The year built, tier rating, and individual tenant names for this location are not published by the operator.
